title: AI Cybersecurity Threats: New Playbook Needed | WEF | World Economic Forum
gist: Very thin 134-word WEF video blurb: Kat Duffy (Council on Foreign Relations) argues AI brings new speed and scale to cyber threats but not new problems, and calls for a government-private sector international framework for cooperation, knowledge-sharing and enforcement. No data or detail beyond the pitch.

themes.theme: AI as accelerant of existing cyber threats

insights.claim: Kat Duffy of the Council on Foreign Relations argues AI-enabled cyber threats differ from past ones in speed and scale rather than in kind, so the problems themselves are not fundamentally new.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Implies existing security controls remain relevant but must be rebuilt for volume and velocity; incumbents' tooling is scaled, not obsolete.
insights.quote: We're talking about new speed, we're talking about new scale, we are not necessarily talking about new problems.

insights.claim: As AI grows in power and scale, opportunities expand for actors who use it as a weapon or tool for criminality, and the global response is not yet keeping pace.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A policy-response lag points to rising cyber loss and compliance spend before coordinated enforcement catches up.
insights.locator: As AI increases in power and scale

insights.claim: Duffy calls for a new government-private sector partnership: an international framework for cooperation, knowledge-sharing and enforcement against AI-enabled cyber threats.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Signals direction of policy travel: expect more cross-border information-sharing mandates and obligations on private firms.
insights.quote: What’s needed is a new partnership between governments and the private sector - an international framework for cooperation, knowledge-sharing and enforcement.
insights.locator: What's needed is a new partnership

insights.claim: Duffy claims the world already knows how to build such a framework, implying existing cooperation models can be adapted rather than invented anew.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Suggests faster adoption potential than a greenfield regime, though the text gives no specifics on which models.
insights.locator: the world already knows how to build it

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum's Global Future Council for Cybersecurity convenes experts to improve organizational cyber resilience and establish governance to safeguard digital societies and economy.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Indicates the WEF channel as a venue where cyber governance norms are being shaped.
insights.locator: The World Economic Forum's Global Future Council
